Upgrading and rolling back

Source: vignettes/articles/upgrading.Rmd
upgrading.Rmd

What is pinned

Every image is pinned to a release tag or, where a project publishes no releases, to a digest. The current set:

Component Version
I-SPI 1.3.3
i-spi-compute API and worker 1.2.0 (curveRcore 0.7.1, curveRfreq 0.5.2, curveRbayes 0.5.2, curveRweights 0.3.1, CmdStan 2.40.0)
Database schema (calib schema) 0.7.1

The automated checks fail if an ImmunoPlex image is not pinned, or if the Kubernetes manifests and the Compose file use different versions.

I-SPI’s About page (in its sidebar) shows the running I-SPI version, the database’s calib schema version, and which compute releases produced the stored results.

Upgrading

  1. Read what changed: I-SPI’s CHANGELOG.md, and for i-spi-compute its tags and the README in worker/migrations/.
  2. If the new i-spi-compute release brings a new calib schema version, apply its migration to the existing database before starting the new worker. Migrations are in i-spi-compute’s worker/migrations/, with instructions in that folder’s README. The table schema_version records which version the database holds.
  3. Change the image tags in the manifests (i-spi.yml, i-spi-compute.yml, and i-spi-compute-sim.yml if used) and apply them. On the local stack, change local/docker-compose.yml and run docker compose up -d.
  4. Check the About page.

The schema files in db/ are only for a new, empty database. Do not load them into a database that already has data.

From I-SPI 1.1.1 and i-spi-compute 1.1.1 to I-SPI 1.3.3 and i-spi-compute 1.2.0

  1. Database: calib schema 0.7.1. i-spi-compute 1.2.0 writes new columns of calib_weights_fit (the options of the additive weights fit and its fit diagnostics). Before starting the 1.2.0 worker, take a pg_dump and apply migration 012_calib_weights_fit_options.sql. It only adds columns (ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS) and records version 0.7.1 in schema_version, so running it twice is harmless.
  2. I-SPI environment: new names. In i-spi.yml (and local/docker-compose.yml) rename db, db_host, db_port, db_userid_x, db_pwd_x to DB_NAME, DB_HOST, DB_PORT, DB_USER, DB_PASSWORD; the values stay the same. I-SPI 1.3.3 still reads the old names if the new ones are missing, and says so in its log, so the rename can follow the image change.
  3. Optional: set ISPI_ENABLE_ADDITIVE_WEIGHTS: "true" on I-SPI to offer the additive precision-weights model. It needs the 1.2.0 worker.
  4. Change the image tags and check the About page: I-SPI 1.3.3, calib schema 0.7.1, and new jobs recorded under i-spi-compute v1.2.0.

From i-spi-compute 1.1.0 to 1.1.1

The 1.1.0 worker stored no back-calculated standard or control estimates for Bayesian fits saved without posterior draws (the default). After upgrading, fill them in from the stored fits; nothing is refitted. Find the affected curves:

SELECT s.curve_id
FROM madi_results.calib_standards s
JOIN madi_results.calib_fit f
  ON f.curve_id = s.curve_id AND f.method = s.method AND f.is_best
WHERE s.method = 'bayesian'
GROUP BY s.curve_id
HAVING bool_and(s.pcov IS NULL AND s.predicted_log10_concentration IS NULL);

Then run i-spi-compute’s worker/backfill_point_estimates.R for those curves only, with the worker’s DB_* environment, first with --dry-run:

Rscript backfill_point_estimates.R --method bayesian --curve_ids 101,102,103 --dry-run
Rscript backfill_point_estimates.R --method bayesian --curve_ids 101,102,103

Pass --curve_ids: without it the script also revisits every Bayesian curve that has no control wells.

Rolling back

Apply the previous image tags. A rollback of I-SPI or of the worker alone does not touch the database.

The migrations so far only add tables, columns and views, so older images keep working with a newer schema: I-SPI 1.0.0 runs against calib schema 0.7.0. A migration cannot be undone by changing images; restore from a database backup if you need the old schema itself. Take a pg_dump before every migration.
